newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thais remain keen on investing in Burma -- survey.
newsitem.headline: Thais remain keen on investing in Burma -- survey.

text.p: A majority of Thai businessmen surveyed remain keen on investing in military-ruled Burma, despite political conflicts and other problems there, a Thai research group said on Friday.

The Thai Farmers Research Center said 54.2 percent of Thai investors questioned had expressed strong interest in doing business in Burma, while only 25 percent were reluctant to invest under current political conditions.
Burma is ruled by the military-led State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) which seized power after crushing pro-democracy uprisings in September 1988.

The military junta is faced with demands for more freedom and democracy from Burmese opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi and has been criticised by Western countries for refusing to accept the demands.

Thai Farmers Research said that while many investors surveyed were not bothered by the military dictatorship, they found the existence of corruption in the controlled Burmese market, a confusing foreign exchange system and a lack of credible official data to be major disincentives.

Most Thai investors already in the Burmese market are engaged in the services sector, while those keen on making new investments were interested in agri-business, goods distribution, manufacturing and other services.

Burma's abundant natural resources, market size and potential for strong economic growth were cited as key factors attracting Thai investors, Thai Farmers Research said. Most of the respondents said they needed Thai government support to boost their competitiveness in Burma. Support they wanted included soft loans, credible economic data and help in negotiations, it added.
Thai investments in Burma currently totalled $960.2 million, the group said.
